message.title: Samsung Reportedly Ramps 4nm Capacity For Memory Chips, Stepping Up Competition With SK Hynix, Micron
message.body: Samsung has allocated more than half of its existing 4nm capacity to HBM4 base-die production, according to South Korean outlet MoneyTodayThe company’s HBM revenue share climbed to 33% in Q2 from 21% in Q1, narrowing the gap with SK Hynix.Rising AI infrastructure spending could leave the HBM market undersupplied next year, creating room for Samsung to gain further share.Samsung Electronics is preparing to expand its advanced foundry capacity as surging demand for next-generation memory chips pushes its 4-nanometer production lines toward full utilization, according to South Korean business outlet MoneyToday. The move could intensify competition with SK Hynix and Micron as the three memory giants battle for share of the booming AI-chip market.  On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for MU and SKHY was ‘neutral’ as of early Tuesday.Samsung Expands Memory CapacitySamsung is considering expanding its 4nm foundry capacity to support production of HBM4 base dies, the logic layer that sits underneath the DRAM stack and connects the memory to AI accelerators, according to the report.Unlike SK Hynix, which uses TSMC’s 12nm process for its HBM4 base die, Samsung is manufacturing the component in-house using its 4nm process.Samsung has already allocated more than half of its current 4nm capacity to HBM4 base-die production, according to MoneyToday. Demand is also coming from other customers, including Nvidia’s Groq 3 LPU, prompting Samsung to raise prices for new 4nm orders.  HBM Race Gets More CompetitiveThe capacity push comes as Samsung accelerates its HBM4 ramp. The company expects HBM4 revenue to more than triple sequentially in the third quarter and for HBM4 to account for more than 60% of its total HBM revenue in the second half.Samsung’s gains are already reshaping the competitive landscape. Counterpoint data showed Samsung’s HBM revenue share rose to 33% in the second quarter from 21% in the first, while SK hynix held 50% and Micron 18%.  The company is also considering a new 2nm production line for HBM5, whose base die is expected to use a 2nm process. That could further strengthen Samsung’s vertically integrated approach, combining memory, logic manufacturing and advanced packaging.Pressure On SK Hynix, MicronFor SK Hynix and Micron, Samsung’s faster HBM4 ramp creates another competitive challenge just as AI infrastructure spending drives unprecedented demand for high-bandwidth memory.TrendForce reported in June that Samsung was the first supplier to complete HBM4 validation and begin shipments, while SK hynix faced qualification delays and Micron remained more focused on HBM3E.  Citi expects global HBM bit demand to rise 62% next year, potentially leaving the industry undersupplied. That means Samsung’s capacity expansion could allow it to capture a larger slice of a rapidly growing market. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com.

novelty.reason: The reference view contains Q1 HBM shares and general Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron HBM competition, as well as Micron's HBM4 shipment milestones. This message adds Samsung's reported allocation of more than half of existing 4nm capacity to HBM4 base dies, the Q2 share shift to Samsung 33% and Micron 18%, and Samsung's further HBM4/HBM5 capacity plans.

policy.reason: The message does not satisfy any existing Policy condition. It reports competitor capacity and market-share changes but not the required consecutive Micron internal combination, ASP, bit-shipment, or company-confirmed qualification and delivery deterioration.

expert_trade.expectation_delta: New Q2 market-share data places Micron at approximately 18% while Samsung rose from 21% to 33%, and Samsung is allocating more than half of its existing 4nm capacity to HBM4 base dies with additional ramp plans. This lowers the expected share and relative pricing/mix capture available to Micron, even though aggregate HBM demand may remain undersupplied and Micron's absolute HBM revenue can still grow.
expert_trade.prior_expectation: Micron's baseline was that HBM4 high-volume shipments and severe AI-memory undersupply would support continued high-value data-center mix, pricing, and HBM share capture; Micron held approximately 21% of global HBM revenue in Q1 2026.
expert_trade.reason: TRADE SHORT: The competitor's capacity commitment, HBM4 commercial progress, and Micron's relative share decline create a non-trivial negative surprise in the HBM value-capture path. HBM and data-center mix are material to Micron's ASP and margin outlook, and the transmission is competitor capacity and share gain -> lower Micron HBM share/pricing power -> weaker relative revenue and mix capture. The single-quarter, third-party share data and strong market growth limit certainty but do not remove the directional edge.

canonical_events.title: Micron expanded multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements and supply commitments
canonical_events.canonical_summary: Micron's multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements used take-or-pay, quantity and price-band terms, customer commitments and reserved capacity to increase forward demand and pricing visibility; reported client coverage included automotive, data-center, consumer-device and industrial customers, and Micron reported that long-term agreements covered approximately 20% of DRAM bits and 33% of NAND bits.
canonical_events.known_event_summary: 2026-08-31..2026-09-21 Micron strategic-customer-contract update: sixteen agreements and roughly $22 billion of commitments or deposits, price floors/bands and reserved 2027 capacity were described; the latest report said long-term agreements covered about 20% of DRAM bits and 33% of NAND bits.

canonical_events.title: Micron FY2026 Q3 results and FY2026 Q4 guidance
canonical_events.canonical_summary: Micron's FY2026 third-quarter release reported record revenue, profitability, cash generation and segment results, and set the FY2026 fourth-quarter operating baseline. The release and immediate follow-up also described four very large Strategic Customer Agreement customers, projected that executed SCAs could account for at least half of revenue, indicated moderating price increases in FY2026 Q4 guidance, and reported a $325 million debt-prepayment loss.
canonical_events.known_event_summary: 2026-06-24 Micron FY2026 Q3 earnings release: revenue was about $41.46 billion, gross margin was about 84.6%-85%, EPS was $24.67, FY2026 Q4 revenue guidance was near $50 billion with adjusted gross margin near 86%, price-increase momentum was expected to moderate, and results included a $325 million debt-prepayment loss; the call also described four very large SCA customers and projected executed SCAs could represent at least half of revenue.
